newsitem.title: ITALY: Private industry lukewarm on Italy budget.
newsitem.headline: Private industry lukewarm on Italy budget.

text.p: Italian employers' association Confindustria has praised the government's efforts to pass a tough 1977 budget but criticised the package for not making key cuts to pension and healthcare benefits.
"The first overall indications on the 1997 budget bill are not sufficient to draw a complete conclusion," Confindustria president Giorgio Fossa was quoted as saying in financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore.

"While we appreciate the government's efforts to reduce the deficit to allow Italy to join the first group of countries in a single European currency, we are puzzled by the composition of the package," he said.

"An important opportunity has been lost to correct structural imbalances in pension and healthcare spending which will, in any case, need to be reduced if Italy wants to remain in the European Union," he added.

The government, which approved its 1997 budget on Friday, shelved plans to tax pensions and raise charges for hospital treatment after the hard-left Communist Refoundation party threatened to scupper the budget in parliament.
The centre-left government relies on support from the Marxist-inspired party in the lower house Chamber of Deputies.

The budget will cut a total of 62.5 trillion lire ($41.12 billion) off next year's public sector deficit, aiming to reduce Italy's deficit to gross domestic product (GDP) ratio to three percent by the end of next year.
Achievement of the three percent deficit target would put Italy on course to join a group of countries establishing a single European currency in 1999.
